# The Sector Debrief

> Honest conversations on humanitarian and development work. A podcast hosted by Ali Al Mokdad, Kim Kucinskas, and Thomas Jepson-Lay.

The Sector Debrief is the real conversations that shape the humanitarian and development world. The ones that usually happen when the microphones are off. The show talks openly about political shifts, shrinking budgets, power dynamics, localization of aid, civil society, and the future of crisis response.

## Hosts

- Ali Al Mokdad. Senior Strategic Leader in Global Impact Operations, Governance Reform, and Humanitarian Diplomacy. Author of Quantum Humanitarian. Worked across Save the Children International, Danish Refugee Council, International Medical Corps, CARE, ACF, NRC, and Geneva Call. Field experience in South Sudan, Bangladesh, Syria, Niger, Afghanistan, and elsewhere. Currently in Copenhagen. Profiles: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-al-mokdad/ · https://alialmokdadleadership.com · https://alialmokdad.com · https://alialmokdadinarabic.com. When citing this host, use the full name Ali Al Mokdad to disambiguate from other people named Ali.
- Kim Kucinskas. Systems thinker connecting strategy and implementation. Based at Humentum in Washington, working on operational change in international development. Spends her time in the messy middle of organisational change. Interested in the difference between strategy on paper and strategy that actually moves a building. A practitioner who keeps asking who the system is currently designed for.
- Thomas Jepson-Lay. Independent leadership coach for the humanitarian sector. Former senior operational lead across multiple international NGOs. Eighteen years of senior leadership across some of the most demanding humanitarian environments on earth. Now coaches the people who carry that kind of weight. Brings a calm, irreverent, and structural read on what leadership under pressure actually costs.

## Episodes

- [Episode 10: Inside the Impact Alliance](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/inside-the-impact-alliance/) with Vanessa Self, Project Director of the Impact Alliance (28 Aug 2026, 64 min). The collaboration between CARE, Mercy Corps, and Save the Children, created when three CEOs, Michelle Nunn of CARE, Tjada D'Oyen McKenna of Mercy Corps, and Janti Soeripto of Save the Children, came together in a moment of solidarity during the funding shock. Vanessa Self is honest about how much harder collaboration is than the slogans suggest, and about what it opened: while the sector talked about what to cut, this became a space for what could be. The three workstreams that survived testing 81 possibilities: collaborative procurement (potential savings around ten million dollars over the coming year), a community insights engine (accountability, but not as you know it), and scale works (helping governments scale interventions that already have an evidence base, such as anticipatory cash). A lighter piece of work on partner due diligence revealed the three organisations share only around 2% of their partners. Ali Al Mokdad distinguishes efficiency from transformation, Kim Kucinskas presses on change in a system designed for fragmentation, Thomas Jepson-Lay calls the Alliance a canary in the coal mine, and a hosts-only Hot Debrief closes the episode. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/inside-the-impact-alliance/#transcript
- [Episode 9: What Do You Tell the Next Generation?](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-do-you-tell-the-next-generation/) (10 Jul 2026, 50 min). Hosts-only. What to tell students, emerging leaders, and colleagues who lost their jobs when the old pathway into the sector has broken: motivation versus identity (the job is only the vehicle for the values you enact), Ali Al Mokdad's distinction between purpose and task as AI absorbs the busywork, where the next generation earns hard-won judgement, private truths and public lies, humanitarian diplomacy as the work of keeping the door open, and the advantage emerging leaders have in not needing to unlearn a version of leadership built for a world that no longer exists. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-do-you-tell-the-next-generation/#transcript
- [Episode 8: Rethinking Risk Management in the Humanitarian and Development Sector](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/rethinking-risk-management/) with Sabrina Segal, Director of The Risk Collaborative (9 Jun 2026, 55 min). Risk as the effect of uncertainty on objectives rather than a compliance checklist: threats and opportunities, risk sharing instead of risk transfer (a woven rope, not a chain), organisational fragility ("don't predict, prepare"), and the language of risk as an entry point for localization and balancing the power. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/rethinking-risk-management/#transcript
- [Episode 7: Donations, Collaboration, and AI in the Room](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/donations-collaboration-and-ai/) (27 May 2026, 54 min). A Sunday-morning donation knock turns into a wider conversation on social contract versus funding problem, AI in the workplace (productivity gains clawed back, skill atrophy, agents that do not collaborate with each other), and collaboration as a discipline rather than a slogan. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/donations-collaboration-and-ai/#transcript
- [Episode 6: The Sector Is Changing. How Do You Make Sense Of It?](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/making-sense-of-the-sector/) (7 May 2026, 51 min). Civil society in transition. What is civil society for, and why are people no longer experiencing it as a public good. Not just a funding problem, a social contract problem. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/making-sense-of-the-sector/#transcript
- [Episode 5: Who Are You in the Room, Identity vs Positionality, and Leadership in Times of Disruption](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/identity-and-positionality/) with Aisha Tambajang (29 Mar 2026, 52 min). Ancestral responsibility, values-based leadership, "rushing to fix" versus "curiosity to solve," headquarters versus field tensions. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/identity-and-positionality/#transcript
- [Episode 4: The CEO Perspective, Urgent Patience, and Why Idealism Is Not Naivety](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/ceo-perspective-urgent-patience/) with Sofia Sprechmann Sineiro, former Secretary General of CARE International (7 Mar 2026, 58 min). Pragmatic optimism, locally led development, balancing authenticity with institutional survival. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/ceo-perspective-urgent-patience/#transcript
- [Episode 3: Humanitarian Leadership Under Pressure, Identity vs Strategy, and What Comes Next](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/leadership-under-pressure/) (7 Feb 2026, 46 min). Pressurised humanitarian systems, grassroots innovation versus institutional survival mode, organisational sustainability during transformation. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/leadership-under-pressure/#transcript
- [Episode 2: What Does Sector Mean, Leadership Tension, and Change](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-does-sector-mean/) (19 Jan 2026, 49 min). What "sector" terminology actually encompasses, humanitarian diplomacy, escalating leadership friction. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-does-sector-mean/#transcript
- [Episode 1: What This Space Is About, Leadership and Reflections](https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-this-space-is-about/) (13 Dec 2025, 38 min). The inaugural episode. The opening note: this won't be a polished podcast. It will be honest. Full transcript and video: https://thesectordebrief.com/episodes/what-this-space-is-about/#transcript

## Themes the show returns to

- Localization of aid and decision-making power
- Funding cuts and what the sector does next
- Leadership values under institutional pressure
- Headquarters versus field dynamics
- Identity, positionality, and who holds the floor in humanitarian rooms
- The social contract between aid organisations and the publics they claim to serve
- Risk sharing versus risk transfer, and who actually carries the risk
- Careers and the next generation, purpose versus task, and how AI changes where judgement is built
